---
title: Events and reports
description: Drain what the engine has to tell you, see what it missed, and read what each node of the graph cost.
---

The engine never calls you back. It keeps a ring of events and you drain it,
which means nothing arrives on a thread you weren't expecting and no handler
runs in the middle of a frame you were still using.

## Draining

```c
goss_event events[32];
uint32_t count = 0;
uint64_t dropped = 0;

goss_session_poll_events(session, events, 32, &count, &dropped);
```

Drain once per frame after submitting. You're already on the right thread at
the right moment.

## The dropped count is the signal

`dropped` is how many events were lost since your last drain because the ring
filled up. It's the clearest early warning that your app isn't keeping up, and
reading it costs nothing.

Surface it somewhere. If you log a climbing dropped count you get a few seconds
of warning before anything visible goes wrong. If you throw the number away,
you find out from a user.

<Warning>
A binding that doesn't expose `dropped` has thrown away the only backpressure
signal there is. Pass it through even if your first integration ignores it.
</Warning>

## Firing your own

```c
goss_session_fire_event(session, ...);
```

A lens can react to events your app raises, which is how you wire your own
moments into what draws without the lens knowing anything about your code.

## Reports

Reports tell you what actually happened on the last frame. Read these instead
of wrapping calls in your own timers.

```c
goss_session_report_frame(session, ...);   /* this frame */
goss_session_read_report(session, ...);    /* the session */
goss_engine_read_report(engine, ...);      /* the engine */
goss_session_chain_report(session, ...);   /* the active chain */
```

Per node, when you need to know which part of the graph is costing you:

```c
uint32_t nodes = 0;
goss_session_node_report_count(session, &nodes);
for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nodes; i++) {
    goss_session_node_report_at(session, i, &report);
    goss_session_node_report_id(session, i, &id, &id_len);
}
```

This loop answers "what's slow" with a name. A wall clock around a submit tells
you the frame took eight milliseconds. The node report tells you which node
spent six of them.

## What to do with reports in a product

- **In development**, draw them. A small overlay showing spent against budget
  and the most expensive node pays for itself in the first week.
- **In CI**, assert on them. If a pull request moves a node's cost, it should
  have to say so.
- **In production**, sample them. You don't need every frame, and a number from
  a real device beats anything you measure at your desk.
